title: Pronouns: the big picture
topic: lo, la, le, se, double pronouns in the present and the past
why: This review lesson brings together all the pronouns seen since A1 (reflexive, direct, indirect, double) and runs them through every tense and form the learner knows, from the present to the imperative. It closes the pronoun unit with step-by-step replacement exercises and a dialogue about a surprise birthday party.

All the pronouns at a glance

You now have all the pieces of the puzzle. Here's the complete table:

Direct or indirect? Ask the question

  • \"Whom? What?\" → direct: Veo la película → la veo.
  • \"To whom?\" → indirect: Escribo a Marta → le escribo.

English \"him\" and \"her\" won't help you here, since \"I help her\" and \"I ask her\" look exactly the same. A few verbs to watch:

VerbSpanishEnglish
ayudar a alguienla ayudo (direct)I help her
llamar a alguienlo llamo (direct)I call him
invitar a alguienlos invito (direct)I invite them
preguntar a alguienle pregunto (indirect)I ask him / her
gustar, encantarle gusta (indirect)he / she likes it
dolerle duele la cabeza (indirect)he / she has a headache

The a before a person doesn't mean \"indirect\"! It's often just the \"personal a\" (Conozco a Marta). Only the question \"to whom?\" counts: ayudar a Marta = to help Marta → la ayudo.

", "

Replacing step by step

Take a sentence and replace the nouns one at a time:

Regalo un reloj a mi padre. → Le regalo un reloj. → Se lo regalo.I'm giving my father a watch. → I'm giving him a watch. → I'm giving it to him.

Here's the same sentence in every tense and form you know:

FormSentenceTranslation
presentSe lo regalo.I give it to him.
perfectoSe lo he regalado.I've given it to him.
indefinidoSe lo regalé ayer.I gave it to him yesterday.
imperfectoSe lo regalaba cada año.I used to give it to him every year.
ir a + infinitiveSe lo voy a regalar. / Voy a regalárselo.I'm going to give it to him.
gerundSe lo estoy envolviendo. / Estoy envolviéndoselo.I'm wrapping it for him.
tú imperativeRegálaselo.Give it to him.
usted imperativeRegáleselo.Give it to him. (formal)

Watch the gender: English just says \"it,\" but el reloj is masculine, so lo. The pronoun always matches the gender of the Spanish noun.

The participle doesn't change

Good news: just like in English (\"the flowers, I've given them\"), the participle after haber never changes: ¿Las flores? Se las he regalado. Never \"regaladas\"!

¿Las invitaciones? Ya las he enviado.The invitations? I've already sent them.
", "

Traps to avoid

  • Le lo doesn't exist. Before lo, la, los, las, le and les turn into se: Se lo digo.
  • Indirect first. \"I give it to him\" is se lo doy, and \"you tell it to me\" is me lo dices.
  • Both pronouns together. Te lo voy a dar or voy a dártelo, never one pronoun on each side.
  • Accents. Two pronouns on an infinitive (dártelo), one or more pronouns on a gerund (haciéndolo), the imperative of a verb with more than one syllable (cómpralo).
  • The double. Le escribo a mi madre sounds natural; and when an object comes first, you repeat it with a pronoun: A mi madre le escribo, El pan lo compro yo.

Leísmo in Madrid

In Madrid, you'll often hear le instead of lo for a man: A Pablo le conozco desde niño (instead of lo conozco). It's accepted for a male person, but you should use lo: it's always correct.

Reflexive se, or the se of se lo?

Pablo se pone el jersey. → Se lo pone.Pablo puts on his sweater. → He puts it on.
Doy el jersey a Pablo. → Se lo doy.I give the sweater to Pablo. → I give it to him.

In the first example, se is the pronoun of ponerse (the verb is in the 3rd person); in the second, it replaces le (the verb is in the 1st person). The verb always tells you which one it is.
